summary: Established an AIDE-based file integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (AlmaLinux 9). Installed aide via dnf, initialized the database against the distro-default config (which explicitly covers ~100 critical /etc paths plus a catch-all /etc PERMS rule), activated it as /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz, and validated detection by modifying and reverting /etc/issue (AIDE correctly reported the change with exit code 4 and exact hash/size diffs, then reported clean after revert). Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-restart boot_id and a clean AIDE check, issued `systemctl reboot` with the ack returning before disconnect, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed, and verified the AIDE database and integrity check both survived and remain functional post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (AlmaLinux 9.6) and confirmed dnf availability
Reviewed /etc/aide.conf default rules confirming comprehensive /etc coverage
Ran aide --init to build the baseline database (28662 entries)
Activated the baseline by moving aide.db.new.gz to aide.db.gz
Ran aide --check confirming a clean baseline (no differences)
Modified /etc/issue, re-ran aide --check to prove change detection (exit 4, diff details shown), then reverted the file and confirmed clean state again
Captured pre-restart boot_id and AIDE db checksum as baseline
Issued a backgrounded systemctl reboot on node1 so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed, indicating an actual restart
Re-verified AIDE db checksum unchanged and aide --check still reports a clean /etc baseline post-restart

evidence.requirement: AIDE installed and integrity baseline database initialized for /etc
evidence.summary: Confirmed AlmaLinux 9 with dnf, installed aide, reviewed default config's extensive /etc coverage, and ran aide --init producing a 28662-entry database in ~5s.

evidence.requirement: Baseline database activated and confirmed clean against current /etc state
evidence.summary: Moved aide.db.new.gz to aide.db.gz and ran aide --check, which reported 'NO differences between database and filesystem'.

evidence.requirement: Baseline proven functional by detecting a real change to /etc and confirming revert restores clean state
evidence.summary: Appended a line to /etc/issue; aide --check exited 4 and reported the exact file, size change (23->47 bytes), and hash diffs. After reverting /etc/issue, aide --check again reported no differences.

evidence.requirement: Healthy pre-restart baseline captured on node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 82d4f0d1-b4b2-494f-8b25-851ee6e6dec7, boot time, and md5 of the AIDE database prior to restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 2 && systemctl reboot' returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately, before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Connection reset was observed mid-reboot (cmd-dcd31a941f16451a), then polling succeeded with a new boot_id 0659a87b-24ff-4f3b-8b14-bd054391a4f6, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, confirming an actual reboot occurred.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of the integrity baseline verified
evidence.summary: After restart, the AIDE database md5 (9f02adc21b5c85aca11215df2c3d8e95) matched the pre-restart checksum, and aide --check again reported 'NO differences', confirming the baseline and its checking capability persisted through the reboot.
